title: Dress'em in Vests!
statementMd:
The Two-dimensional kingdom is going through hard times... This morning the Three-Dimensional kingdom declared war on the Two-dimensional one. This (possibly armed) conflict will determine the ultimate owner of the straight line.

The Two-dimensional kingdom has a regular army of $*n*$ people. Each soldier registered himself and indicated the desired size of the bulletproof vest: the $*i*$-th soldier indicated size $*a*_{*i*}$. The soldiers are known to be unpretentious, so the command staff assumes that the soldiers are comfortable in any vests with sizes from $*a*_{*i*} - *x*$ to $*a*_{*i*} + *y*$, inclusive (numbers $*x*, *y* ≥ 0$ are specified).

The Two-dimensional kingdom has $*m*$ vests at its disposal, the $*j*$-th vest's size equals $*b*_{*j*}$. Help mobilize the Two-dimensional kingdom's army: equip with vests as many soldiers as possible. Each vest can be used only once. The $*i*$-th soldier can put on the $*j*$-th vest, if $*a*_{*i*} - *x* ≤ *b*_{*j*} ≤ *a*_{*i*} + *y*$.

## Input

The first input line contains four integers $*n*$, $*m*$, $*x*$ and $*y*$ ($1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 10^{5}$, $0 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ 10^{9}$) — the number of soldiers, the number of vests and two numbers that specify the soldiers' unpretentiousness, correspondingly.

The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) in non-decreasing order, separated by single spaces — the desired sizes of vests.

The third line contains $*m*$ integers $*b*_{1}, *b*_{2}, ..., *b*_{*m*}$ ($1 ≤ *b*_{*j*} ≤ 10^{9}$) in non-decreasing order, separated by single spaces — the sizes of the available vests.

## Output

In the first line print a single integer $*k*$ — the maximum number of soldiers equipped with bulletproof vests.

In the next $*k*$ lines print $*k*$ pairs, one pair per line, as "$*u*_{*i*}$ $*v*_{*i*}$" (without the quotes). Pair ($*u*_{*i*}$, $*v*_{*i*}$) means that soldier number $*u*_{*i*}$ must wear vest number $*v*_{*i*}$. Soldiers and vests are numbered starting from one in the order in which they are specified in the input. All numbers of soldiers in the pairs should be pairwise different, all numbers of vests in the pairs also should be pairwise different. You can print the pairs in any order.

If there are multiple optimal answers, you are allowed to print any of them.

## Note

In the first sample you need the vests' sizes to match perfectly: the first soldier gets the first vest (size 1), the third soldier gets the second vest (size 3). This sample allows another answer, which gives the second vest to the fourth soldier instead of the third one.

In the second sample the vest size can differ from the desired size by at most 2 sizes, so all soldiers can be equipped.
statementZhMd:
二维王国正经历艰难时期……今天早晨，三维王国向二维王国宣战。这场（可能会武装起来的）冲突将决定直线的最终归属。

二维王国拥有一支由 $*n*$ 名士兵组成的正规军。每名士兵都进行了登记，并说明了自己想要的防弹背心尺寸：第 $*i*$ 名士兵指定的尺寸为 $*a*_{*i*}$。众所周知，士兵们并不挑剔，因此指挥部认为，对于第 $*i*$ 名士兵来说，尺寸在 $*a*_{*i*} - *x*$ 到 $*a*_{*i*} + *y*$（含边界）之间的任何防弹背心都可以接受（其中 $*x*, *y* ≥ 0$ 是给定的数）。

二维王国拥有 $*m*$ 件防弹背心，第 $*j*$ 件防弹背心的尺寸为 $*b*_{*j*}$。请帮助动员二维王国的军队：为尽可能多的士兵配备防弹背心。每件防弹背心只能使用一次。如果满足 $*a*_{*i*} - *x* ≤ *b*_{*j*} ≤ *a*_{*i*} + *y*$，则第 $*i*$ 名士兵可以穿戴第 $*j*$ 件防弹背心。

## 输入格式

第一行包含四个整数 $*n*$、$*m*$、$*x*$ 和 $*y*$（$1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 10^{5}$，$0 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ 10^{9}$），分别表示士兵数量、防弹背心数量，以及表示士兵不挑剔程度的两个数。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*a*_{*1}, *a*_{*2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$），由单个空格分隔，按非递减顺序排列，表示士兵想要的防弹背心尺寸。

第三行包含 $*m*$ 个整数 $*b*_{*1}, *b*_{*2}, ..., *b*_{*m*}$（$1 ≤ *b*_{*j*} ≤ 10^{9}$），由单个空格分隔，按非递减顺序排列，表示可用防弹背心的尺寸。

## 输出格式

第一行输出一个整数 $*k*$，表示能够配备防弹背心的士兵数量的最大值。

接下来的 $*k*$ 行中，每行输出一对整数，格式为 "$*u*_{*i*}$ $*v*_{*i*}$"（不含引号）。二元组（$*u*_{*i*}$，$*v*_{*i*}$）表示第 $*u*_{*i*}$ 名士兵必须穿戴第 $*v*_{*i*}$ 件防弹背心。士兵和防弹背心的编号均从 1 开始，按照它们在输入中的顺序编号。各二元组中的士兵编号必须两两不同，防弹背心编号也必须两两不同。可以按任意顺序输出这些二元组。

如果存在多个最优答案，可以输出其中任意一个。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，需要使防弹背心的尺寸完全匹配：第一名士兵得到第一件防弹背心（尺寸为 1），第三名士兵得到第二件防弹背心（尺寸为 3）。本样例还存在另一种答案，即将第二件防弹背心分配给第四名士兵，而不是第三名士兵。

在第二个样例中，防弹背心尺寸与期望尺寸最多可以相差 2，因此所有士兵都可以配备防弹背心。
